subject: agent-editeur-canvas
verdict: Lean stateless agent with strong persona; critical eval gap and orphaned build artifact need attention.
summary: Trace is a focused, well-characterized canvas editor with a clear persona and tight capability prompts. The primary weakness is an eval suite with only 2 cases (critical), and a prompt-quality-canon.md that inflates context without being routed. The persona is treated as investment and preserved.

agent_profile.name: Trace
agent_profile.title: Éditeur canvas
agent_profile.mission: Traduire une instruction utilisateur en modifications concrètes sur le canvas Excalidraw

capabilities.name: apply-instruction
capabilities.note: Translate user instruction into Excalidraw canvas changes

capabilities.name: integration-fun
capabilities.note: Wire Trace into Fun Chat and diagram pipeline

detailed_analysis.leanness: Lean overall — two redundancy findings in SKILL.md/apply-instruction.md, one canonical issue; validate-excalidraw.md and integration-fun.md are tight.
detailed_analysis.architecture: Clean stateless skill — frontmatter, topology, progressive disclosure, and activation all pass; one low-severity finding on reference frontmatter divergence.
detailed_analysis.determinism: Minor over-structure in apply-instruction.md; otherwise destination-focused.
detailed_analysis.customization: Metadata-only customize.toml, no override surface — acceptable for stateless agent with focused scope.
detailed_analysis.enhancement: Lean core with critical eval gap and one misallocated reference; no hostile-environment or headless guidance.
detailed_analysis.agent-cohesion: Lean, well-carved skill; orphaned canon reference and missing on-activation config parity.

journeys.name: Canvas edit
journeys.steps: User opens diagram → asks Trace to modify → Trace produces Excalidraw JSON → Rust validates and saves → canvas updates

journeys.name: Review redirect
journeys.steps: User asks for review → Trace redirects to relecteur-diagramme

themes.title: Over-documented wiring, under-documented contract
themes.root_cause: apply-instruction.md mixes LLM guidance with Rust pipeline plumbing and numbered process steps. validate-excalidraw.md describes validation as if the agent runs it, but Rust handles it. This confuses the model about its actual role.
themes.action: Reframe apply-instruction.md as goal + non-inferables only. Reframe validate-excalidraw.md as the Rust validation contract, not agent behavior.

themes.title: Build artifact pollution
themes.root_cause: prompt-quality-canon.md (1652 tokens, 2.7× SKILL.md) was auto-copied by the builder. It's a meta-document about prompt authoring, never routed, never loaded by the agent. It inflates context on every activation.
themes.action: Remove references/prompt-quality-canon.md from this skill. It belongs to the builder root.

themes.title: Thin eval coverage
themes.root_cause: Only 2 eval cases for a skill that handles add/remove/relabel/recolor/reposition/connect. No edge-case, error, or hostile coverage.
themes.action: Add 6+ eval cases covering invalid JSON rejection, ambiguous instruction, delete of absent element, empty diagram, non-French input, and non-edit routing.

themes.title: Missing personalization and fallback
themes.root_cause: On-activation doesn't load user config ({user_name}, {communication_language}). No fallback for non-edit or non-French inputs.
themes.action: Add config loading to On Activation. Add catch-all routing for non-edit intents.

strengths: Strong, specific persona — 'artisan visuel précis' is memorable and functional
Clean stateless topology — everything in SKILL.md + 3 focused references
Tight non-inferables — JSON validity, canvas editability, Tauri persistence clearly stated
Communication style table encodes non-obvious mappings (ambiguous instruction, invalid JSON)
Integration-fun.md cleanly describes the wiring without bloating SKILL.md

recommendations.action: Remove references/prompt-quality-canon.md — orphaned build artifact inflating context by 2.7×
Add 6+ eval cases to cases.json covering edge cases, errors, and hostile inputs
Reframe apply-instruction.md: collapse numbered steps to outcome statement, remove Rust plumbing description
Reframe validate-excalidraw.md as Rust-side validation contract, not agent behavior
Add config loading ({user_name}, {communication_language}) to On Activation and catch-all routing for non-edit intents

findings.title: Overview restates name+description
findings.evidence: The overview sentence restates what the YAML name+description already convey.
findings.recommendation: Replace overview with the outcome-only mission line and cut the restated role description.

findings.title: Approach prescribes process instead of stating outcome
findings.evidence: Four numbered steps script the route. A model that knows the outcome and non-inferables already knows to parse intent and confirm.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to outcome statement. Cut numbered steps and confirm step.

findings.title: Minimal diff principle restated across files
findings.evidence: Same rule in two files.
findings.recommendation: Keep in SKILL.md, remove restatement from apply-instruction.md.

findings.title: Reference frontmatter uses non-standard fields
findings.evidence: code and type fields in reference frontmatter are inert.

findings.title: Numbered steps in apply-instruction.md
findings.evidence: Four numbered steps form a scripted sequence.

findings.title: Plumbing description in apply-instruction.md
findings.evidence: Describes Rust pipeline flow not needed for LLM decision-making.

findings.title: Missing consumer in apply-instruction.md
findings.evidence: No explicit consumer specified.

findings.title: Eval suite has only 2 cases
findings.evidence: Only trigger-edit and baseline-separation. No edge-case, error, or hostile coverage.
findings.recommendation: Add 6+ cases covering invalid JSON, ambiguous instruction, delete-missing, empty canvas, non-French input, non-edit routing.

findings.title: validate-excalidraw.md describes agent-side validation that never runs
findings.evidence: Non-Inferables says validation runs in Rust, but Approach reads as if the agent performs it.
findings.recommendation: Reframe as Rust validation contract. Remove agent-side checklist.

findings.title: prompt-quality-canon.md is meta-reference, not operational guidance
findings.evidence: 1652 tokens, never routed, never loaded. Inflates context on every activation.
findings.recommendation: Remove from this skill. Belongs to builder root.

findings.title: SKILL.md activation duplicates identity and communication style
findings.evidence: Identity, Communication Style, and On Activation carry overlapping info.

findings.title: No guidance for non-edit or non-French inputs
findings.evidence: Routing table lists French edit verbs only.
findings.recommendation: Add catch-all routing for non-edit intents.

findings.title: .memlog.md mixes languages
findings.evidence: Chinese text in an English/French context.

findings.title: No headless invocation contract
findings.evidence: No input schema for headless callers.

findings.title: No override surface in customize.toml
findings.evidence: Metadata only, no override hooks.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable for focused stateless agent. Document if needed.

findings.title: Hardcoded persona and routing in SKILL.md
findings.evidence: Name, emoji, language, routing verbs hardcoded.

findings.title: Hardcoded error strings in references
findings.evidence: Error message hardcoded inline.

findings.title: prompt-quality-canon.md is orphaned build artifact
findings.evidence: 1652 tokens, never routed, dead weight.

findings.title: On-activation missing config loading
findings.evidence: Doesn't load {user_name}, {communication_language} like sibling skill.

findings.title: Only two eval cases for multi-operation skill
findings.evidence: Handles 6 operations, tests 2.
